entries.1.43: 'Look, Laksmana, at the woods laden with blossom now that the winter is over. To me their flowers are of no use at all.
entries.1.45: 'The birds call out sweetly in flocks, full of joy, as though inviting one another. For me they only quicken the madness of love.
entries.1.81: 'Shalmalis and kimshukas, red kuravakas too, tinishas and naktamalas, chandanas and syandanas —

entries.2.18: 'You are endowed with intelligence and discernment. Go about it all by reading their gestures, for a king who has lost his judgement cannot govern any of his subjects.'
entries.4.6: 'There was a king named Dasaratha, brilliant and devoted to dharma, who always ruled the four classes each according to its own duty.
entries.4.9: 'This hero is the most virtuous of Dasaratha's sons, endowed with every royal mark and possessed of royal fortune.
entries.4.10: 'Fallen from the kingdom, he has come here with me to dwell in the forest.

entries.9.2: 'When our father died, the ministers held that he was the elder and made him lord of the monkeys in the kingdom, with the consent of all.
entries.9.15: 'Well over a year passed for him after he had entered the cavern, and that whole time went by for me as I waited at its mouth.
entries.9.17: 'Then after a long while I saw red blood flow out of that cavern with foam upon it, and I was overcome with grief.
entries.10.21: 'As he lay roaring upon the ground, the blood pouring from his mouth filled that cavern until it could no longer be crossed.
entries.10.22: 'Having slain that valiant enemy, the son of Dundubhi, I found as I came out that the mouth of the cavern had been closed.
entries.11.3: 'Listen with an undivided mind to Vali's manliness, his valour and his fortitude, and then do what is to be done thereafter.

entries.13.18: 'Here dwelt seven sages called the Saptajanas, strict in their vows and disciplined, lying immersed in the water with their heads downward.

entries.17.16: 'Rama is tender of heart, devoted to the welfare of his people, compassionate, of unfailing energy, one who knows the fitting time and is steadfast in his vows.
entries.17.17: 'Such is the fame that all creatures upon the earth speak of you.
entries.17.20: 'You ought not to have struck me while I was engaged with another and off my guard. Such was the thought that arose in my mind when I could not see you.

entries.18.13: 'The elder brother, the father, and he who imparts knowledge — these three are to be known as fathers by those who walk the path of righteousness.
entries.18.14: 'The younger brother, one's own son, and a pupil of good qualities — these three are to be regarded as one's sons, for dharma is the measure in this.
entries.18.33: 'A thief is absolved of his theft either by punishment or by release, but a king who does not punish an offender takes that sin upon himself.
entries.18.47: 'A lesser man cannot argue with one so distinguished. Raghava, if I spoke unfitting and unpleasant words earlier out of ignorance, you should not hold me at fault for that either.
entries.21.10: 'A son has been provided for, and whatever now remains to be done for the king should all be carried out. Such is the decision the hour demands.'
entries.21.14: 'I have no authority over the king of the monkeys, nor over Angada. Sugriva, his father's brother, comes next in all matters.'
entries.22.5: 'Take up this very day the kingdom of these forest dwellers, and know that this very day I go to the abode of Vaivasvata.

entries.24.43: 'The three worlds do not overstep the order ordained, for they are subject to it. You shall attain that supreme happiness, and your son shall receive the office of heir apparent. Such is the order the Creator has ordained, and the wives of heroes do not give way to lamentation.'
entries.27.45: 'A hero repays a kindness with a kindness in return. The ungrateful man who returns no favour breaks the heart of the spirited.
entries.28.60: 'Seeing that the season forbade any march, that the roads were very hard to travel, and that Sugriva was loyal to me, I said nothing at all.
entries.28.62: 'Sugriva, having rested, will himself know when the time has come and will remember the help he received. Of that there is no doubt.'
entries.29.33: 'Whichever vanara fails to arrive here beyond fifteen nights shall suffer the penalty of death, and there is to be no debating it.'
entries.30.37: 'The mud has dried under the advancing heat of the sun, and the earth throws up thick dust long pent up. Now is the season of effort for kings who bear enmity toward one another.
entries.31.6: 'No man of your kind in this world would commit such a wrong. He who destroys evil by noble means is a hero and the best of men.
entries.32.19: 'Raghava, roused to anger, is able by lifting his bow to bring the whole world under his sway, gods, asuras and gandharvas together.

entries.35.22: 'Thousands of crores of bears and hundreds of golangulas will come to you this day. Give up your anger, subduer of enemies. Many crores of monkeys of fiery spirit will come, Kakutstha.
entries.37.15: 'Let those who know the ways go swiftly and, learning where they are, bring in at my command all the monkeys upon the earth.'
entries.37.36: 'All the mountains, the oceans and the forests have been covered, and at your command all the vanaras upon the earth are coming.'
entries.38.22: 'A king intent upon slaying his enemies and given to winning friends, who enjoys the fruits of the three ends of life, is joined with righteousness.
entries.40.9: 'This task of theirs is indeed known to me in principle. Even so, you should give the command as it ought properly to be given.'
entries.41.25: 'There above all Sita must be sought with every effort, for that region is the dwelling of the evil-minded Ravana, lord of the demons, who deserves to be slain and whose splendour equals that of the thousand-eyed one.
entries.41.28: 'Beyond that island, a hundred yojanas out in the sea, stands a splendid mountain named Pushpitaka, frequented by siddhas and charanas.
entries.42.33: 'Beyond that lord of mountains lies a mountain all of gold, its caves golden within and its slopes set with streams and waterfalls.
entries.42.34: 'Elephants and boars, lions and tigers roar about it on every side without ceasing, made proud by the sound of their own voices.
entries.43.35: 'There lies the lake called Vaikhanasa, covered with golden lotuses and moved over by auspicious swans bright as the rising sun.
entries.43.36: 'Kubera's royal mount, the elephant known as Sarvabhauma, roams that place always in the company of his cow elephants.
entries.44.4: 'All the worlds are known to you, with their asuras and gandharvas, their nagas, men and gods, their seas and their mountains.

entries.46.12: 'Then, pursued by that Vali, I fled, and as I ran I saw many rivers and forests and cities pass beneath me.
entries.46.13: 'Then the earth appeared to me like the surface of a mirror, like the circle traced by a whirling firebrand, and small as the print of a cow's hoof.
entries.49.4: 'Much time has passed for us, and Sugriva is stern in command. Therefore let all of you search together upon every side.
entries.49.8: 'The fruit of work steadily done is certainly seen. Enough of yielding to despair, for it is not fitting that we should close our eyes to the task.
entries.49.14: 'Let all of you search the forest and every mountain fastness everywhere, in all the places pointed out by the great Sugriva.'
entries.52.6: 'That king's friend is a heroic vanara named Sugriva, king of the foremost among monkeys, and it is by him that we were sent forth.
entries.52.9: 'Having searched the whole of the southern quarter, we were all worn out and hungry, and took shelter at the foot of a tree.
entries.53.3: 'Lady, you should bring us out of this dreadful cavern. We have overstepped Sugriva's command and our lives are forfeit.'
entries.53.8: 'Close your eyes, all you bulls among vanaras, for it is not possible to get out with the eyes unclosed.'
entries.53.23: 'You have won his trust, you are skilled in the ways of policy, devoted to your master's welfare, and were sent forth with instructions for every task.

entries.58.33: 'That flesh-eater who did so despicable a deed deserves retaliation from me, for the enmity my brother incurred has become my own.
entries.60.5: 'When I recovered consciousness after six nights I was helpless and bewildered, and though I looked about in every direction I could recognise nothing at all.

entries.60.20: 'You are the elder, Sampati, and Jatayu is your younger brother. Assume human form, both of you, and touch my feet.
entries.63.12: 'Make every effort by all means, and you will trace Sita. This regaining of my wings is for you a token that you will succeed.
entries.65.13: 'Know what my range is now, altered as it is by the passing of the years. I can leap ninety yojanas, and of that there is no doubt.
entries.65.22: 'Dear one, a master who sends others is never himself one to be sent. Best of the leaping monkeys, all this company is yours to send.
entries.66.8: 'There was an apsara named Punjikasthala, renowned as the foremost among apsaras, who came to be known as Anjana, the wife of the monkey Kesari.
entries.66.26: 'When the three worlds were thrown into turmoil all the gods grew uneasy, and the lords of the worlds propitiated the angry Maruta.
entries.67.22: 'Leaping with a composed mind, I shall scatter the clouds, shake the mountains and dry up the ocean.
entries.67.26: 'As I leap across the ocean my form will be like that of Visnu of old, when he strode his three strides.
entries.67.33: 'These chiefs among the monkeys who wish you well have gathered here, and with one mind they will offer prayers for the success of your undertaking.
entries.67.35: 'We shall stand upon one foot until your return, and the lives of all these forest dwellers depend upon you.'
